target: Dyna'r ysgol lle dysgodd hi ddarllen.
english: That's the school where she learned to read.
tip: lle joins a place to what happened there, like where: yr ysgol lle dysgodd hi = the school where she learned.

target: Dwedodd hi taw hi oedd yn gywir.
english: She said it was her who was right.
tip: taw marks a reported emphasis in south Welsh, like that it was: Dwedodd hi taw hi = she said it was her.

target: Dywedodd e am i fi beidio â phoeni.
english: He told me not to worry.
tip: beidio â means not to; after â the next word takes an aspirate mutation, so poeni becomes phoeni in beidio â phoeni.

target: Gofynnodd y myfyriwr a oedd y llyfr ar gael.
english: The student asked if the book was available.
tip: a opens an indirect yes or no question, like whether: Gofynnodd... a oedd = asked whether it was.

target: Baswn i'n trwsio'r to sy'n gollwng cyn i'r gaeaf ddod.
english: I would fix the leaky roof before winter comes.
tip: cyn i means before; the verb after softens, so dod becomes ddod: cyn i'r gaeaf ddod = before winter comes.

target: Pe na bai'n bwrw glaw, bydden ni'n mynd am dro.
english: If it weren't raining, we would go for a walk.
tip: Pe na bai means if it weren't; pe sets an unreal condition and na makes it negative: Pe na bai'n bwrw glaw.

target: Dyma'r diwrnod poetha'r flwyddyn.
english: This is the hottest day of the year.
tip: Add -af for most or -est: poeth (hot) becomes poetha, hottest: y diwrnod poetha'r flwyddyn = the hottest day.

target: A fyddai'n bosib trefnu cyfarfod?
english: Would it be possible to arrange a meeting?
tip: A opens a yes or no question and softens the next word: byddai becomes fyddai in A fyddai'n bosib = would it be possible.

target: Mae dy gar a dy feic yn y garej.
english: Your car and your bike are in the garage.
tip: dy (your) softens the next consonant: car becomes gar and beic becomes feic in dy gar a dy feic.

target: Taw hi oedd yno.
english: That it was her who was there.
tip: Taw fronts a focus clause, a southern form of mai. Taw hi oedd yno stresses it was her, not someone else, who was there.

target: Dw i wedi bwcio ystafell.
english: I've booked a room.
tip: wedi marks a completed action and replaces the present-tense yn: Dw i wedi bwcio = I have booked.

target: Dywedodd neb fod unrhyw broblem.
english: Nobody said there was any problem.
tip: unrhyw (any) triggers soft mutation: problem becomes broblem in unrhyw broblem.

target: Fe oedd wedi awgrymu'r syniad.
english: He suggested the idea.
tip: Fronting the pronoun before oedd marks focus: Fe oedd wedi awgrymu = it was him, not another, who suggested it.

target: Yr ateb yw gweithio gyda'n gilydd.
english: The answer is to work together.
tip: gyda'n gilydd means together; gilydd (each other) takes a possessive matching the group, here 'n for our.

target: Dyna'r pentref lle tyfais i lan.
english: That's the village where I grew up.
tip: lle links a place to a clause as where: Dyna'r pentref lle tyfais i = that's the village where I grew up.

target: Mae'r cyllideb yn pennu gwariant y llywodraeth.
english: The budget determines government spending.
tip: Welsh marks possession by juxtaposing nouns, with no word for of: gwariant y llywodraeth = the government's spending.

target: Dywedodd e y byddai'n ffonio cyn diwedd y dydd.
english: He said he would call before the end of the day.
tip: y byddai carries reported would: Dywedodd e y byddai'n ffonio = he said that he would phone.

target: Mae mis Ionawr yn oer a thywyll yn y gogledd.
english: January is cold and dark in the north.
tip: a (and) triggers aspirate mutation: tywyll becomes thywyll in oer a thywyll = cold and dark.

target: Dywedodd y ferch fod y ffilm yn drist ond yn dda.
english: The girl said the film was sad but good.
tip: The linking yn softens a following adjective: trist becomes yn drist, da becomes yn dda.

target: Hi oedd wedi cynllunio'r ardd.
english: It was her who designed the garden.
tip: A feminine singular noun soft-mutates after the article: gardd becomes 'r ardd = the garden.

target: Mae hi eisoes wedi bwcio'r gwyliau.
english: She has already booked the holiday.
tip: eisoes (already) sits just before wedi: Mae hi eisoes wedi bwcio = she has already booked.

target: Rydyn ni eisoes wedi bwyta'n cinio.
english: We have already eaten our lunch.
tip: 'n before a noun is short for ein (our): bwyta'n cinio = eat our lunch.

target: Dyna'r mynydd dringais i'r haf diwethaf.
english: That's the mountain I climbed last summer.
tip: Welsh often drops the relative word that: Dyna'r mynydd dringais i = that's the mountain I climbed.

target: Cymerodd ein taith yn hirach na'r disgwyl.
english: Our journey took longer than expected.
tip: na means than after a comparative: yn hirach na'r disgwyl = longer than expected.

target: Darllennais i fod y pris wedi codi.
english: I read that the price had risen.
tip: fod means that in reported clauses: Darllennais i fod y pris wedi codi = I read that the price had risen.

target: Ymunodd ein ffrindiau â ni am farbeciw.
english: Our friends joined us for a barbecue.
tip: ymuno takes â (with), not a plain object: Ymunodd ein ffrindiau â ni = our friends joined us.

target: Dw i newydd orffen paentio'r ystafell wely.
english: I have just finished painting the bedroom.
tip: newydd before a verb means have just, and softens it: newydd orffen (from gorffen) = have just finished.

target: Hi oedd wedi fy nysgu i bobi.
english: She taught me to bake.
tip: fy brackets the object and nasal-mutates it: dysgu becomes fy nysgu i = taught me.

target: Derbynnir ceisiadau hyd at ddiwedd mis Mai.
english: Applications are accepted until the end of May.
tip: The -ir ending makes an impersonal passive with no named doer: Derbynnir ceisiadau = applications are accepted.

target: Hi yw'r person ieuengaf i ennill y gadair.
english: She's the youngest person to win the chair.
tip: The -af ending forms the superlative: ieuengaf = youngest, from the irregular ifanc.
